reading.body:
Laura Gillen's AI record is legislative and educational, not infrastructure: five AI bill cosponsorships, four recorded votes, and six PAC contributions, with no event touching data centers, power, or compute.

The pattern is a lawmaker working the workforce and literacy end of AI policy. The cosponsorships run from the AI PLAN Act in March 2025 through the Small Business AI Advancement Act in February 2026, and include the CREATE AI Act, the NSF AI Education Act, and the LIFT AI Act. The recorded votes are all yea, on suspension motions, which is the calendar for broadly agreed bills rather than contested ones. The money is small and corporate: four $1,000 Amazon PAC contributions and three Microsoft PAC entries, two of which are a $1,000 contribution and a matching $-1,000 on the same day in September 2025, which reads as a correction or refund rather than a second transaction.

For AI specifically, this is the part of the policy stack that shapes who can build and use models, not where they run. Compute, buildings, and power do not appear anywhere in these fifteen events. A reader looking for a position on data center siting, grid interconnection, or chip supply will not find one here.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. It holds only events this site has dated, so committee work, statements, and votes not tied to a listed bill are absent. The contributions are from PACs, not the companies directly, and no event establishes that any contribution and any vote are related.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Laura Gillen: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 15 events.
